directProviderComparison.interpretation: One WebView observation after provider metadata batching; direct CacheStorage is a platform control, while provider time also includes SHA verification, manifest-root handling, and content-addressed bookkeeping. It is not a cross-device performance claim.

stressCase: The API 35 WebView profile persisted only the CacheStorage payload bytes while the provider manifest stayed content-addressed and rooted. A full 4-payload fill at half-capacity produced deterministic two-entry residency and two evictions at 8/32/128 KB. The prior per-read manifest persistence path was materially slower in the same provider comparison; the candidate now makes access telemetry persistence explicit and batches concurrent manifest flushes.
boundaries: VSR remains the owner of asset catalog, leases, active working sets, imports, resolution roots and residency receipts; CacheStorage owns only discardable payload bytes and its provider manifest.
The 50 KB Build policy bounds provider cache resident bytes, not the in-memory VSR working set and not the embedded APK payload size; the APK still contains deterministic base64 payloads.

persist_accesses=false makes LRU access telemetry ephemeral across process termination; payload writes still await a manifest flush, and stale access order affects eviction preference only, not world correctness or authority.
https://rncs.local/ is a local synthetic document origin supplied to WebView loadDataWithBaseURL; it is not a remote endpoint, TLS deployment, WAN transport, or network authority.

The API 35 Android ATD result and storage/performance probe are emulator/WebView profile evidence only. They do not establish physical-device behavior, quota guarantees, cross-device coherence, release signing, store delivery, production SLA, or human visual acceptance.
No K400 gate is promoted to PASS; this is candidate runtime evidence only.
donorAdvantage: The existing Node content-addressed cache provider supplied the manifest-root, SHA payload, atomic persistence and deterministic LRU contract; browser and Android remain lowerings/providers rather than new semantic owners.
regressionCase: The pre-lowering file origin exposed CacheStorage and WebCrypto but rejected Cache.put with an unsupported file scheme; synthetic-origin lowering enabled the provider. The subsequent WebView comparison exposed per-read manifest persistence as a shared provider performance bottleneck, which is now explicit and bounded by policy.
nextCandidate: Repeat the quota/eviction/performance receipt on a reproducible physical target profile, then assess remote content-addressed cache coherence. External transport remains separately blocked on canonical protocol, donor licensing, TLS/key custody and cross-node authority decisions.
